# 🧬 Adaptive Synthetic Data Augmentation Toolkit

A closed-loop ML engine that **detects the exact cohorts your model fails on**,
generates **targeted** synthetic data to fix them, and proves the gain on a
held-out test set — benchmarked against SMOTE.

## 🚀 What it does
1. Splits your data **three ways** (train / validation / test) with stratification.
2. Trains a baseline classifier, tunes its decision threshold on validation, and
   finds the subpopulations whose recall is **genuinely below** the model's
   overall recall (ranked by recoverable false negatives) — not merely where
   false negatives concentrate.
3. Fits per-cohort `GaussianCopula` / `TVAE` / `CTGAN` synthesizers (via SDV) on
   the **real** rows of each weak cohort — **once**; later iterations only draw
   fresh samples (fitting dominates runtime, sampling is cheap).
4. Runs an adaptive loop: generate → quality-gate → augment → retrain → evaluate,
   **re-detecting weak cohorts whenever the model improves** so each iteration
   targets the *current* model's failure modes.
5. Derives extra **candidate models** each iteration from the same augmented
   data: a probability-**calibrated** model (synthetic rows shift the
   probability scale; calibration restores it) and **baseline⊕augmented
   ensembles** at several blend weights (the baseline keeps global ranking, the
   augmented model brings cohort recall). The best candidate wins on validation.
6. Selects the best iteration on **weak-cohort recall** (validation), guarded so
   global F1 can't silently degrade beyond a tolerance you set. Global metrics
   (PR-AUC / ROC-AUC / F1) are available as alternative selection objectives —
   with the ensemble candidates, global-metric selection can beat the baseline
   on *every* test metric at once.

   **Two recommended modes** (set via *Selection metric* + *Threshold policy*):
   - **Max cohort repair** — `cohort_recall` + `max_f1`: biggest weak-cohort
     recall lift; global precision dips a little by design (the F1-optimal
     threshold spends the model's gains on recall).
   - **Nothing falls** — `pr_auc` + `match_baseline_precision`: candidate
     thresholds maximise recall *while holding the baseline's precision*, so
     precision, F1, PR-AUC and ROC-AUC are all held or improved and the weak
     cohorts still gain. Use this when stakeholders watch global metrics.
7. Reports the final lift **once** on the untouched **test set** — including a
   per-cohort recall table (baseline vs best) — next to no-augmentation,
   random-oversampling, and **SMOTE** baselines.

## 🧪 Try it in 30 seconds
`testing.csv` ships with the repo: a 1,600-row synthetic churn dataset with a
planted weak cohort (positives in `region = West` are deliberately borderline,
baseline recall ≈ 0.08–0.39 there). Upload it, pick target `churn`, train the
baseline, run the loop — and watch the West cohort's test recall multiply while
global metrics hold.

## ✨ Why it's trustworthy
- **No data leakage.** Cohort detection and model selection use validation only;
  the test set is evaluated a single time for the final number.
- **No model collapse.** Generators are always re-fit on *real* cohort data, so
  the loop never learns from its own synthetic output.
- **Honest labels.** Synthetic rows are drawn from real rows of the *intended
  class*, not relabeled after the fact.
- **Quality-gated.** Each synthetic batch is scored (KS / total-variation
  fidelity) and low-quality batches are rejected.
- **The right objective.** Targeted augmentation lifts recall *inside* weak
  cohorts but rarely moves global AUC — selecting on a global metric hides the
  real effect. The default objective is mean weak-cohort recall with an
  explicit global-F1 guardrail, so trade-offs are chosen, not accidental.
- **Fair thresholds.** Every model (baseline, SMOTE references, and each
  iteration) gets its decision threshold tuned on validation the same way.
- **Benchmarked.** Every run shows whether adaptive augmentation actually beats
  plain SMOTE on the same held-out test set.

## ⚙️ Installation
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## 🎮 Run the dashboard
```bash
streamlit run app.py
```
Open `http://localhost:8501`, upload a CSV, pick a **binary** target column, set
your generator/loop parameters, then **Initialize & Train Baseline** → **Run
Optimization Loop**. Export the augmented dataset, the best model, and a
Markdown run report from the results panel.

## 🧪 Tests
```bash
pytest -q
```
The suite covers target encoding, the 3-way split, cohort sampling/labeling,
quality scoring, and a full leakage-free end-to-end loop.

## 📦 Project layout
| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `data_utils.py` | Ingestion, cleaning, target encoding, 3-way split, preprocessing |
| `models_utils.py` | Model factory + binary metrics (incl. PR-AUC) |
| `generator_utils.py` | Per-cohort SDV synthesis + fidelity scoring/gating |
| `loop_engine.py` | Streaming adaptive loop + SMOTE/oversampling references |
| `app.py` | Streamlit dashboard |
| `tests/` | pytest suite |

> Note: SDV caps generator fitting at 5,000 rows per cohort for speed; very large
> CSVs are loaded fully into memory, so size your inputs accordingly.
